newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil Search seen making Discovery bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil Search seen making Discovery bid.

text.p: Oil Search Ltd had taken the first step in a likely takeover bid for Discovery Petroleum NL with the revelation that the Papua New Guinea-based producer was conducting due diligence, corporate advisers said.
Discovery, which has assets in Indonesia and Australia, said it would consider bids of at least 86 cents per share -- six cents per share above the latest bid by Premier Oil Plc.
"Oil Search...are going through the same sort of due diligence process that Premier did," Discovery managing director Eric Streitberg told Reuters.
Asked if Oil Search was likely to make a bid, he said: "They are certainly holding discussions with us and verifying the (Australian and Indonesia portfolio) data just like Premier have done."
In an earlier statement, Discovery said the latest offer by Premier was still at the lower end of the 77 to 95 cent range set in independent experts report by merchant bank Grant Samuel.

Arguing that the valuation contained a lot of blue sky, Premier said its A$106.5 million offer was 14 percent above its initial bid and represented full value. Premier spokesman Steve Lowden said another hike in the the bid was unlikely.
"We are relying on the independent experts valuation," Streitberg said, when asked what he thought was a fair price.
"That was a range of 77 to 95 cents and the mid-point was 86 and we will consider any bid that we get in that context," he said.
The share market, which has constantly overbid Premier's offer, pushed Discovery shares to a day's high of 81 cents before it ended three cents higher at 80 cents.
"We know that there have been some arbs (arbitrageurs) in there buying the stock," said a corporate adviser involved in the current takeover discussions.

"The market is expecting a higher bid and it is expecting it for two reasons," the adviser said. "The market is expecting Oil Search to do something and secondly they are probably also saying -- 'hey, Premier you are a bit light on here'."

Oil Search, whose main asset is a stake in the Kutubu oilfield, already ranks as the largest shareholder in Discovery with a 10.1 percent holding which was purchased after the original bid by Premier at a price of 75 cents per share.
Oil Search managing director Peter Botten was not available for comment, with his Port Moresby office saying he was travelling around Australia.

Oil Search has described Discovery as a well-managed company with exploration and development potential, particularly in Southeast Asia. "We have been looking at Discovery for some time as we look to diversify our risk profile and buy other production assets," Botten said on September 30.
Discovery has an 18.75 percent interest in Indonesia's Kakap gas field.

Premier was wary about the valuation placed on the company's Australian exploration assets in Western Australia's Perth and Carnarvon Basins. Its offer for a minimum of 50.1 percent closes on December 11. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
